key_insight: SELDON trains a continuous-time deep latent ODE variational model to learn supernova explosion light-curve dynamics, enabling millisecond-scale probabilistic forecasting and parameter inference instead of hours-long MCMC runs.
problem_solved: Current physics-based inference pipelines cannot scale to the ~10 million optical transient alerts per night expected from LSST/Rubin Observatory; SELDON provides fast, scalable, and uncertainty-aware inference from irregular, multi-band time-series.
method: Continuous-time latent model: encoder → latent Neural ODE → decoder to model light-curve dynamics in continuous time.
Variational (amortized) inference to produce fast approximate posteriors and predictive uncertainty for each event.
Training on simulated/observed supernova light curves to handle irregular sampling and multi-band data, enabling real-time forecasting and parameter estimation.
impact: Practitioners can replace slow MCMC with a deployable, millisecond-scale probabilistic model for transient classification, prioritization, and automated follow-up decisions at survey scale.
visual_elements: Model architecture diagram: encoder mapping observations to latent state → latent Neural ODE evolution → decoder producing continuous-time light curves and uncertainties.
Latency comparison bar chart: MCMC (hours) vs SELDON (milliseconds) per object.
Example multi-band light curves showing observed points, SELDON reconstructions, and predictive uncertainty bands over continuous time.
Pipeline flow: high-rate alert stream → SELDON inference → real-time classifications/priorities for follow-up (icons for telescope, compute, alert broker).
paper_title: SELDON: Supernova Explosions Learned by Deep ODE Networks
paper_authors: Jiezhong Wu, Jack O'Brien, Jennifer Li, M. S. Krafczyk, Ved G. Shah
